name: Roppongi
description: Roppongi from open data, lit by the real sun: Roppongi Hills under Mori Tower with Maman the spider and the Mohri Garden, Keyakizaka's winter lights, the National Art Center's glass wave, Tokyo Midtown, and the bars round the crossing.

imagery.attribution: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) seamless aerial photographs (GSI terms of use, source attribution)

terrain.attribution: GSI Fundamental Geospatial Data DEM5A, 5 m airborne laser survey bare earth (GSI terms of use); 10 m DEM where 5A is absent

terrain_check.name: GSI elevation API (1 m laser DEM where flown, otherwise DEM5)

plateau.attribution: MLIT Project PLATEAU Tokyo 23 wards LOD2 building models (CC BY 4.0), as vector tiles by indigo-lab (MIT)

seawall.note: The rivers' and the bay's revetments and the castle moats: granite blocks and concrete.

trees.note: Species are not mapped, and the shared trees have no ginkgo or cherry, so the mix stands in: elms for the zelkovas (keyaki) of Keyakizaka and the gardens, plane trees for the street planes and ginkgos, maples for the Mohri Garden and Midtown's. A guess, not a survey.

tour.title: Roppongi, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's 5 m laser-scanned bare earth.

tour.title: Roppongi Hills
tour.text: Mori Tower, 238 m, and at its foot Maman, Louise Bourgeois's spider; Keyakizaka's zelkovas lit blue and white in November and December.

tour.title: The art triangle
tour.text: The National Art Center's glass wave, Tokyo Midtown, and the bars of the crossing between them. The signs there are typical of the street, not its real shops'.

sources.landmarks: Maman (Louise Bourgeois, 1999; Mori Building: 9.27 m by 10.0 m) at OpenStreetMap's position; the National Art Center, Tokyo (Kisho Kurokawa, 2007) on its footprint, its glass front's waves from photographs; Keyakizaka's illumination after Mori Building's seasonal programme. The bars' signs are indicative: typical trades, no real shops' signs.
sources.fonts: Signs drawn with Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License: Zen Kaku Gothic New, Dela Gothic One, Bebas Neue, Shippori Mincho

night.note: The bars' signs and Keyakizaka's LEDs are lit landmark meshes (city.py); the streets' lamps are the country's defaults.

weather.source: Tokyo (Kitanomaru Park): Japan Meteorological Agency, 1991-2020 normals, days with at least 0.5 mm

game.title: Roppongi on Foot
game.blurb: Walk Roppongi under the real sun: under the spider at Roppongi Hills, down Keyakizaka's lit avenue, to the National Art Center's glass wave and Midtown, and back to the bars of the crossing.

npcs.name: Ken 健
idle: Roppongi: embassies up the hill, bars down the street, and the last train at half past midnight.
Every country in the world drinks in this square kilometre. {time}.

npcs.name: Erika 恵里花
idle: The art museum is on the 53rd floor. The highest gallery in the world, they say, open till ten at night.
The garden down there was a samurai lord's. The pond is older than everything else here.

npcs.name: Mei 芽衣
idle: 21_21 Design Sight is Tadao Ando's: a steel roof folded like a sheet of paper.
The art triangle: Mori, Midtown, the National Art Center. One ticket stub gets a discount at the others. {sun_line}

npcs.name: Akio 昭夫
idle: No collection of our own. Only exhibitions: twelve galleries, and the building itself is the best exhibit.
The glass wave was the last thing Kurokawa saw finished. He died that year.

quests.title: Roppongi
talk: Welcome to Roppongi. By day, art; by night, this.
Go and meet Erika under the spider at Roppongi Hills. Everybody meets under the spider.

quests.title: Under the spider
talk: Maman: look up at her. Then walk down Keyakizaka; in November the trees are wound in lights.
At the bottom of the hill you can see Tokyo Tower, framed by the avenue.

quests.title: The art triangle
talk: Midtown's garden, then across to the National Art Center. Akio works there; ask him about the glass.
The wave is best at four, when the sun is low behind you.

steps.text: Find Akio at the National Art Center

quests.title: The glass wave
talk: Stand back and look at it: glass louvers in a wave, leaning out as they rise.
Inside, the restaurant floats on top of a concrete cone. Kurokawa liked his cones.

steps.text: Look at the National Art Center's glass wave
